entries.title: Resource detail title markup corrupted the desktop page layout
entries.expected: The title should remain in the document head and the resource heading, tag list, preview and inspector should render as separate layout regions.
entries.actual: Astro split the interpolated title at the slug expression, placing the closing title/head tags before the trailing text. The browser then parsed resource-header children incorrectly and reduced the preview to 237px at 1280px.
reproduction: Open /resources/ai-prompt-hero/ at 1280x900.
Inspect the document title and resource preview; the title was truncated, the detail DOM was misnested and the preview was too narrow.
entries.rootCause: The Astro template split one title string across multiple text/interpolation segments containing parentheses. The compiler hoisted closing head markup between those segments, corrupting all following body markup.
entries.remediation: Render each resource document title as one Astro expression; align both resource-detail routes on the same semantic header and min-width-safe responsive grid.

entries.title: The canonical Dialog resource made standalone exports fail TypeScript build

entries.remediation: Use a single-column workspace modifier when an activity feed has no data-table sibling; retain the two-pane layout for the flagship dashboard pair.

entries.title: Employee dashboard invented onboarding and team-pulse values
entries.expected: Summary values should come from the supplied brief or be identified as illustrative examples.
entries.actual: The employee dashboard displayed an invented count of 12 onboarding journeys and a Positive team-pulse result.
reproduction: Open /compose at 1440x900.
Enter the flagship employee-experience brief and compose.
Inspect Direction A's Team Overview KPI cards.
entries.rootCause: The employee content binder inserted plausible-looking count and sentiment values that were not present in the brief or backed by data.
entries.remediation: Use only the 500-person count provided in the brief and mark the remaining values Example / Illustrative only.

entries.title: E-commerce conversion CTA used onboarding copy and a missing route
entries.expected: Storefront conversion actions should use commerce-specific wording and open a generated product screen that exists in the selected project.
entries.actual: Every e-commerce direction used “Continue onboarding” and linked to #screen-overview, which was absent from the generated screen graph.
reproduction: Open /compose at 1440x900.
Compose benchmark brief ECOM-01.
Inspect the Storefront Catalog preview in Directions A, B, and C.
Activate the primary conversion CTA and inspect the selected screen.
entries.rootCause: The archetype content binder had no e-commerce CTA label or destination rule, so it fell through to a generic onboarding label and overview-screen fragment.
entries.remediation: Bind e-commerce conversion copy to “View product details” and resolve the target against the generated Product Detail screen ID; cover route existence in the semantic benchmark and visible Compose UI test.

entries.title: Returns portal brief generated a storefront purchase flow
entries.expected: A returns portal should let customers find a previous order, request eligible returns, and follow refund status.
entries.actual: The generated ProductModel retained a generic shop objective and planned Storefront Catalog, Product Detail, Checkout, and Order Confirmation screens.
reproduction: Open /compose at 1440x900.
Compose benchmark brief ECOM-06 without an archetype override.
Inspect Product Architecture and each direction’s visible screen selector.
entries.rootCause: The interpreter used the single generic ecommerce archetype for explicit returns-portal intent; it had no domain specialization, so the screen planner inherited a new-purchase funnel.
entries.remediation: Specialize explicit returns-portal briefs within the existing ecommerce archetype, with Order Lookup, Return Request, and Refund Status screens, return/refund workflows, accurate CTA copy, and a visible UI regression.

entries.title: Feature Bento rendered an empty card when composition supplied three items
entries.expected: A flexible feature section should render only supplied items and adapt its grid without an empty card.
entries.actual: The resource always rendered four cards; with three bound items the last card had no heading or description and showed only decorative dots.
reproduction: Open an ecommerce storefront preview with three bound entities, or /resources/feature-bento/.
Set the Feature Bento items prop to three meaningful entries.
Inspect the fourth card at desktop or mobile width.
entries.rootCause: FeatureBento treated its four-card visual fixture as a required fixed contract even though the public items prop accepts arbitrary array length and composition commonly supplies three entities.
entries.remediation: Render cards only when an item is present and choose a balanced grid for one, two, three, and four items; exercise a three-item state in the isolated Sites Worker preview.

entries.title: Returns request disable message was replaced by a generic backend tooltip
entries.expected: A disabled returns action should name the returns service the user must connect.
entries.actual: The button correctly remained disabled but its title said only to connect a generic backend.
reproduction: Open /compose at 1440x900.
Compose the ECOM-06 returns portal brief and inspect Direction A, Return Request.
Inspect the disabled Submit return request button title.
entries.rootCause: A shared disabled-action fallback unconditionally overwrote the returns-specific title assigned by the content binder.
entries.remediation: Preserve the returns-service explanation for the returns submit action and assert the exact disabled-state title in semantic and visible UI regressions.

entries.title: Returns request screen duplicated the primary navigation
entries.expected: A returns request screen should show the product navigation once and reserve its form area for the request.
entries.actual: Direction C rendered the same Order Lookup, Refund Status, and Return Request links in both the sidebar and a second top navigation.
reproduction: Open /compose at 1440x900.
Compose ECOM-06 and inspect Direction C.
Select Return Request and compare the sidebar and content-area navigation.
entries.rootCause: The screen planner inherited the generic settings-nav role for the returns request form; its resource mapped to a product-level top navigation containing the same links as the enclosing sidebar.
entries.remediation: Omit the settings sub-navigation role for explicit returns request screens while retaining the shell navigation; assert one rendered nav and the absence of the inappropriate role.

entries.title: Ordinary activity feeds rendered notification-inbox controls
entries.expected: An overview or activity stream should show a chronological timeline; notification actions should be reserved for explicit notification, inbox, or alert screens.
entries.actual: SaaS Overview Dashboard used notification-centre and displayed the unrelated ‘Mark all as read’ control.
reproduction: Open /compose and enter the SAS-01 brief: A cloud workspace helps a 120-person design consultancy plan client projects, assign ownership, review milestones, and control access by team role.
Compose and inspect Overview Dashboard in Direction A at desktop or mobile size.
Observe the activity panel resource and its inbox action.
entries.rootCause: The activity-feed resource contract allowed both timeline and notification-centre, while composition only forced timeline for consumer briefs and Direction C. Other activity screens were left to scoring and could receive inbox semantics.
entries.remediation: Resolve activity-feed to timeline by default and filter to notification-centre only when the screen name explicitly identifies Notifications, Inbox, or Alerts. The benchmark and visible browser regression now check all three directions at desktop and mobile sizes.

entries.title: Generated activity examples exposed sequence numbers and internal workflow IDs
entries.expected: Sample events should be clearly labeled as examples and use readable, user-facing activity language.
entries.actual: The SaaS overview showed ‘Step 1’ and another direction exposed raw values such as ‘send-invites’ and ‘configure-workspace’.
reproduction: Open /compose and enter the SAS-01 design-consultancy workspace brief.
Compose and inspect the Overview Dashboard activity panel in Directions A and C.
Read the event timestamp, title, and detail copy.
entries.rootCause: Generic activity binding presented workflow array position as a timestamp and copied workflow step identifiers directly into user-facing event details.
entries.remediation: Label generated timestamps ‘Example’, humanize workflow titles and step labels, and assert that examples contain no sequence labels or raw identifiers.

entries.title: Activity panel repeated the enclosing screen heading
entries.expected: An activity panel should have its own useful contextual heading instead of repeating the screen's title.
entries.actual: The Overview Dashboard screen header, KPI section, and notification panel were all titled ‘Overview Dashboard’.
reproduction: Open /compose and enter the SAS-01 design-consultancy workspace brief.
Compose and inspect the Overview Dashboard in Direction A.
Compare the screen header and activity panel heading.
entries.rootCause: The generic content-binding fallback assigned screen.name to activity-feed title when no domain-specific title existed.
entries.remediation: Give ordinary activity panels the heading ‘Recent activity’, with contextual headings for community, employee, returns, and explicit notification screens.

entries.title: Brokerage terminal brief inherited retail banking workflows
entries.expected: A professional brokerage brief should produce market, order-book, position, and trade workflows without retail banking copy.
entries.actual: FIN-05 produced Account Balances, bank statements, and reconcile statements, with raw workflow identifiers in activity details.
reproduction: Open /compose at desktop or mobile size and enter the FIN-05 brokerage terminal brief from the composition benchmark.
Compose and inspect Direction 01 Account Balances and Direction 03 Market Overview.
Observe banking screens, statement copy, or raw workflow IDs.
entries.rootCause: The broad fintech defaults did not specialize explicit trading-terminal, market-depth, and equity-dealer language, so the bank-account workflow was reused.
entries.remediation: Specialize the existing fintech archetype only for explicit trading-terminal intent, create market-specific screens and entities, and bind market events. The 100-brief interpretation and composition benchmarks plus visible desktop/mobile browser flow now reject banking residue.

entries.title: Generated KPI cards used the word Example as a metric value
entries.expected: When no source data exists, metric cards should show an unavailable value and disclose that data is not connected.
entries.actual: The KPI grid displayed Example as the large numeric value for securities, orders, and positions, even though the status said Illustrative only.
reproduction: Open /compose and enter the FIN-05 brokerage terminal brief.
Compose and inspect Market Overview at desktop or mobile size.
Read the large KPI values and their status labels.
entries.rootCause: The shared content binder used a generic Example string for every entity-backed metric rather than representing absent source data explicitly.
entries.remediation: Use an em dash with a truthful data-connection status; distinguish values explicitly supplied by the brief. Render unavailable states with neutral status styling rather than a green success badge.

entries.title: KPI cards cramped long status text into two mobile columns
entries.expected: Small preview widths should use a layout that keeps metric labels and statuses readable without narrow word wrapping.
entries.actual: At 390px, three cards shared two columns and split ‘Market data not connected’ into several short lines.
reproduction: Open /compose at 390x844 and enter the FIN-05 brokerage terminal brief.
Compose and inspect Direction 01 Market Overview.
Observe the KPI grid and the wrapped status labels.
entries.rootCause: The Gold KPI resource always used two columns below its medium container breakpoint, even when the preview column was too narrow for the card copy.
entries.remediation: Use one column for compact containers, two for small/medium containers, and three when the resource has enough width. The browser regression checks actual computed grid columns at desktop and mobile widths.

entries.title: Generic workspace branding repeated the word Workspace
entries.expected: A generated workspace shell should show one coherent brand label and initials that correspond to it.
entries.actual: The SaaS preview labelled its navigation Workspace Workspace and used WW as its avatar mark.
reproduction: Open /compose at desktop or mobile size and enter the SAS-01 consultancy workspace brief.
Compose, open Direction 01, select Overview Dashboard, and inspect the navigation brand and avatar.
entries.rootCause: The content binder always appended Workspace to the first product entity, including when that entity was already named Workspace.
entries.remediation: Use Team Workspace when the inferred entity is only Workspace, retain an existing Workspace suffix, and derive a two-letter avatar mark from the final brand. Red-to-green visible-browser checks cover desktop and mobile.

entries.title: SaaS overview repeated its page heading above the KPI cards
entries.expected: Each major section should have a contextual heading that does not duplicate the page heading.
entries.actual: The Overview Dashboard page header and KPI card section both rendered Overview Dashboard as headings.
reproduction: Open /compose at desktop or mobile size and enter the SAS-01 consultancy workspace brief.
Compose, open Direction 01, select Overview Dashboard, and count the exact Overview Dashboard headings.
entries.rootCause: The content binder fell back to the screen name for metric-card section titles, repeating the page heading in the nested KPI grid.
entries.remediation: Give generic metric-card roles a concise Key metrics heading while preserving employee and returns-specific headings. The 100-brief benchmark rejects metric section titles that repeat their screen heading; the visible browser test checks the rendered heading hierarchy on desktop and mobile.

entries.title: Timeline preview shows the literal word Example where a timestamp should be
entries.expected: Generated sample activity should use readable relative time labels and remain clearly identified as sample content.
entries.actual: Activity feed events displayed Example in the timestamp position, including the SaaS overview preview.
reproduction: Open /compose at desktop or mobile size and enter the SAS-01 consultancy workspace brief.
Compose, open Direction 01, select Overview Dashboard, and inspect the Recent activity timeline.
entries.rootCause: The shared content binder marked generic and domain-specific sample activity with the literal placeholder Example in the time field rendered as a timeline timestamp.
entries.remediation: Use deterministic relative time labels for example activity and conversation events. The 100-brief composition benchmark rejects placeholder timestamps; visible desktop/mobile Compose assertions and screenshots verify the rendered timeline.

entries.title: Real-estate search rendered marketing feature cards
entries.expected: Property search should show real search and listing structure and name a map only when one is present.
entries.actual: Search & Map Explorer rendered generic feature cards without a map or property results.
reproduction: Compose the REA-01 home-search brief.
Inspect Direction 01 and open Search & Map Explorer.
entries.rootCause: The archetype promised an unimplemented map and results-grid resolved to a marketing resource.
entries.remediation: Rename the screen Property Search and bind results-grid to the existing Gold table with truthful property fields.

entries.title: Marketplace search used onboarding copy
entries.expected: Search copy should describe listing discovery and disclose its data connection state.
entries.actual: The search header displayed Continue onboarding and unrelated backend help.
reproduction: Compose the MKT-01 marketplace brief.
Inspect Explore Listings in all three directions.
entries.rootCause: The common search-header binder reused employee onboarding defaults when context copy was absent.
entries.remediation: Use domain-specific labels, placeholders and connection help with a truthful generic fallback.

entries.title: Travel hero repeated its objective
entries.expected: The subtitle should add context without restating the travel objective or implying unsupported booking.
entries.actual: Headline and subtitle repeated generic trip-planning copy.
reproduction: Compose the TRV-01 trip-planning brief.
Compare Direction 01 hero headline and subtitle.
entries.rootCause: Generic hero fallback restated the objective and added a generic booking promise.
entries.remediation: Use concise audience-oriented supporting copy that does not repeat the objective.

entries.title: Filter Builder did not edit conditions
entries.expected: Add Condition should create editable field, operator and value controls.
entries.actual: Rules were static; Add Condition inserted an unrelated canned Category = primitives row.
reproduction: Open /resources/filter-builder/.
Add a condition and try to edit or remove its parts.
entries.rootCause: The add action inserted fixture text rather than managing condition state.
entries.remediation: Create editable blank rows with update/remove actions and disclose that applying rules requires a connected data source.

entries.title: Marketplace results contained unrelated proposal and review rows
entries.expected: Listing search rows should represent listings.
entries.actual: The results contained Proposal and Review records.
reproduction: Compose the MKT-01 marketplace brief.
Inspect the Explore Listings rows in Direction 01.
entries.rootCause: Generic entity-table bindings reused proposal/review entities on a listing-discovery screen.
entries.remediation: Use listing-specific sample records and reject proposal/review rows for marketplace search.

entries.title: Entity rows implied fabricated numeric progress
entries.expected: Without a source measure, table values should be explicitly unavailable rather than numeric.
entries.actual: Generic records displayed invented 0/100 progress values.
reproduction: Compose the MKT-01 brief.
Inspect values and status in Explore Listings.
entries.rootCause: The shared entity fallback formatted absent data as an arbitrary quality percentage.
entries.remediation: Use domain-specific unavailable states and reject numeric scores without source data.

entries.title: Mobile data table clipped important fields
entries.expected: Narrow previews should show each record and its fields without hidden horizontal scrolling.
entries.actual: Later listing columns were offscreen in the mobile preview.
reproduction: Open /compose at 390x844.
Compose MKT-01 and inspect Explore Listings without horizontal scrolling.
entries.rootCause: The shared table used overflow-x at every viewport and had no narrow-screen record layout.
entries.remediation: Keep the keyboard-scrollable table on wide screens and render labeled record cards on mobile.

entries.title: Unavailable values used the success color
entries.expected: Unavailable values should be neutral so users do not mistake them for successful data.
entries.actual: Not connected price and availability values appeared green.
reproduction: Compose MKT-01 or REA-01.
Inspect unavailable data values in the results table.
entries.rootCause: The shared table applied success green unconditionally to displayValue.
entries.remediation: Use neutral text for not-connected/unavailable values in light and dark variants.

entries.title: Employee dashboard marked disconnected metrics with success-green badges
entries.expected: Metrics without a connected data source should use a neutral status treatment so they cannot be read as successful measurements.
entries.actual: The Onboarding and Team pulse cards showed em dashes and ‘No connected data’ inside green success badges.
reproduction: Open /compose at desktop or mobile size.
Enter the exact employee-experience brief and compose.
Open Direction 01, 02, or 03 and select Team Overview.
Inspect the Onboarding and Team pulse status badges.
entries.rootCause: The dashboard KPI renderer classified unavailable statuses by matching ‘not connected’ but the shared content binder emitted ‘No connected data’, so the badge fell through to its green success style.
entries.remediation: Classify common no-data, unavailable, unconfigured, illustrative, and sample states as neutral in the shared KPI resource.

entries.title: Clothing commerce brief composed as a marketing storefront
entries.expected: A direct-to-consumer clothing product should start with product discovery, comparison, sizing, and checkout screens that support the shopping workflow.
entries.actual: The generated plan started with a Storefront Catalog marketing hero and generic order-delivery copy; product search and garment comparison were not represented as the core application workflow.
reproduction: Open /compose and enter the adjudicated benchmark brief recorded in the corresponding benchmark case.
Compose, open Direction 01, and inspect the screen names, navigation and rendered screen content.
Compare the baseline screenshot with the current desktop and mobile captures.
entries.rootCause: The ecommerce archetype defaulted to a Storefront Catalog marketing screen, and the generic planner inherited marketing-page semantics for a product-discovery brief.
entries.remediation: Use a Product Catalog search/explore screen as the ecommerce default and bind the clothing catalog to product-specific search, details, sizing, and order content.

entries.title: Digital music commerce inherited a physical storefront workflow
entries.expected: A licensed music shop should represent album discovery, sample playback, release details, purchase, and digital download.
entries.actual: The music brief received the generic physical storefront and order-delivery plan; the generated workflow did not model licensed albums, sample playback, or downloads.
reproduction: Open /compose and enter the adjudicated benchmark brief recorded in the corresponding benchmark case.
Compose, open Direction 01, and inspect the screen names, navigation and rendered screen content.
Compare the baseline screenshot with the current desktop and mobile captures.
entries.rootCause: The generic ecommerce workflow treated physical goods and digital releases alike and had no music-specific product model or content bindings.
entries.remediation: Specialize music commerce around albums/releases and sample, purchase, and download actions, with matching search and catalog content.

entries.title: Flight management brief planned as a destination and hotel product
entries.expected: A flight-management app should focus on confirmed journeys, flight details, check-in, gate changes, and travel documents.
entries.actual: The generated plan used destination showcase, property detail, and trip itinerary screens, which describe travel discovery and lodging rather than managing confirmed flights.
reproduction: Open /compose and enter the adjudicated benchmark brief recorded in the corresponding benchmark case.
Compose, open Direction 01, and inspect the screen names, navigation and rendered screen content.
Compare the baseline screenshot with the current desktop and mobile captures.
entries.rootCause: Travel interpretation used a broad destination/hospitality architecture for flight operations and did not distinguish confirmed-journey management from trip discovery.
entries.remediation: Detect flight-management intent and specialize its model and screens around confirmed flights, check-in, gates, and travel documents.

entries.title: Film-streaming brief inherited a newspaper publishing architecture
entries.expected: A streaming product should support film discovery, film details, watchlists, and editorial collections.
entries.actual: The generated plan contained a front-page feed, article reader, and section explorer, with journalism copy in the hero.
reproduction: Open /compose and enter the adjudicated benchmark brief recorded in the corresponding benchmark case.
Compose, open Direction 01, and inspect the screen names, navigation and rendered screen content.
Compare the baseline screenshot with the current desktop and mobile captures.
entries.rootCause: The media archetype shared one editorial/news publishing model across news and streaming products without a streaming-specific interpretation.
entries.remediation: Specialize film streaming around catalogue, detail, and watchlist screens, and bind film-specific search and sample data.

entries.title: Destination search used flight-oriented search instructions
entries.expected: A shared trip-planning service should ask users to search destinations and saved places.
entries.actual: The destination search control described journeys/flights and travel details, suggesting an air-travel workflow that the brief did not request.
reproduction: Open /compose and enter the adjudicated benchmark brief recorded in the corresponding benchmark case.
Compose, open Direction 01, and inspect the screen names, navigation and rendered screen content.
Compare the baseline screenshot with the current desktop and mobile captures.
entries.rootCause: The shared search binding used travel-generic copy instead of selecting labels and placeholders from the screen and product domain.
entries.remediation: Bind destination-search labels and placeholders to the destination-planning screen semantics and cover them in the all-directions composition benchmark.

entries.title: Product Catalog could not navigate to Product Detail
entries.expected: A shopper should be able to open the generated Product Detail screen from the Product Catalog in each direction.
entries.actual: The composed project included a Product Detail screen, but its Product Catalog rendered no link to reach it. Digital music catalogs could also target themselves.
reproduction: Open /compose, enter the ECOM-01 clothing-store brief from the reviewed composition benchmark, and compose.
Inspect Direction 01 and select Product Catalog; the initial preview has no Product Detail action.
Repeat for directions 02 and 03; each catalog lacks the discovery-to-detail link.
entries.rootCause: Product Catalog did not require the conversion-cta role, and the music-store target override matched Product Catalog itself instead of Product Detail.
entries.remediation: Require a conversion action on ecommerce Product Catalog screens, bind it to Product Detail with domain-specific product or album wording, and verify the UI navigation at desktop and mobile widths.

entries.title: Dark product canvases made light resource variants unreadable
entries.expected: Resource variants must retain readable text when composed inside a dark Design DNA canvas, with at least WCAG AA contrast for normal text.
entries.actual: Axe found color-contrast failures in 16 of 40 Gold resources using the expressive variant on a dark canvas. Examples measured 1.44:1 for advanced-data-table values, 1.53:1 for an entity-profile badge, 1.65:1 for error text, and 2.20:1 for muted labels on white.
reproduction: Open /compose and enter benchmark brief AI-03.
Compose and open Direction 02, Neural Flow.
Inspect the Support Assistant preview; muted labels on its light timeline panel are nearly unreadable against the dark canvas.
Run the resource contrast regression against all 40 Gold resources with variant=expressive and theme=dark.
entries.rootCause: The renderer applies dark Design DNA semantic text tokens to the screen, while several resource variants render fixed light surfaces. Those resources inherited the dark muted text token; translucent expressive surfaces also mixed with the dark canvas and further reduced contrast.
entries.remediation: Scope semantic muted and secondary text tokens to each resource variant, keeping light variants dark-text-on-light-surface and nocturne light-text-on-dark-surface. Make affected expressive neutral and error surfaces opaque so their declared foreground colors are evaluated against a stable background.

regression.before: The 40-Gold-resource Playwright/Axe sweep failed for 16 resources.
regression.after: 12 focused Playwright/Axe cases passed, and the 40-resource sweep reports zero violations.

entries.title: Scrollable Gold resource panels were not keyboard reachable
entries.expected: Scrollable resource content must be reachable by keyboard with visible focus, and the mobile Gold-resource Axe sweep must have no serious violations.
entries.actual: The CI mobile Axe run reported scrollable-region-focusable violations in error-state, feature-matrix, and three-pane-app-shell. A local mobile reproduction found the feature-matrix and three-pane-app-shell violations.
reproduction: Run pnpm exec playwright test tests/e2e/resource-dark-expressive-contrast.spec.ts --project=mobile-chrome --workers=1.
Before the fix, Axe reports serious scrollable-region-focusable violations for the affected Gold resources.
Tab through the overflowing code sample, comparison table, and workspace canvas; before the fix these regions are skipped.
entries.rootCause: The resource source contained overflow-auto regions without tabindex, accessible names, or visible focus styling, so keyboard users could not reach their scroll controls.
entries.remediation: Make the scroll regions keyboard focusable, give the table and workspace regions accessible names, provide a visible focus outline, and run the all-Gold mobile Axe sweep plus explicit focus regressions.

regression.before: The CI mobile run found three serious violations; the local mobile run found two.
regression.after: The 40-Gold-resource Axe sweep passes on desktop and mobile; six keyboard and responsive browser checks pass.

entries.title: Three-pane app shell clipped its navigation and inspector on mobile
entries.expected: The resource's collapse strategy should keep navigation, workspace canvas, and inspector visible and usable at its declared 360px mobile width.
entries.actual: The fixed 224px and 256px side panes sat beside the canvas inside a 390px hidden-overflow row, clipping part or all of the inspector.
reproduction: Open /preview/?resource=three-pane-app-shell&variant=expressive&theme=dark at 390x844.
Before the fix, the three fixed-width panes remain in one row and the hidden-overflow shell clips the right pane.
Compare with the after screenshot: navigation, workspace canvas, and inspector are stacked vertically, with no horizontal overflow.
entries.rootCause: The implementation kept a desktop-only fixed-width row despite declaring a responsive collapse strategy and phone-width certification.
entries.remediation: Stack panes on small screens, constrain the canvas width, preserve its scroll access, and restore the three-column workspace at the tablet breakpoint.

regression.before: The CSS fixed the side panes at 14rem and 16rem with overflow hidden on the parent row.
regression.after: The mobile layout test confirms all three panes fit within 390px; desktop retains all three columns without overflow.

entries.title: Whitespace-only brief was accepted and generated directions
entries.expected: A brief containing only whitespace should be rejected, explained beside the field, and never produce a Product Architecture or direction cards.
entries.actual: Submitting spaces and line breaks passed the browser required constraint and composed directions from an empty description.
reproduction: Open /compose and wait for Catalogue ready.
Enter spaces and line breaks only, then select Compose Interface System.
Before the fix, no alert appeared and generated direction cards remained visible.
entries.rootCause: The submit handler did not trim or validate the description before calling the deterministic composition pipeline; HTML required validation considers whitespace non-empty.
entries.remediation: Trim the description before composition. Reject empty normalized input, focus the field, and expose an associated alert with aria-invalid.

regression.before: Visible UI browser checks failed on desktop and mobile: no validation alert was shown and directions could be generated from whitespace.
regression.after: Both browser projects reject the input, focus the field, expose an accessible error, and show no direction cards.

entries.title: Edited Compose inputs left directions for the previous brief available
entries.expected: Any change to the brief or design controls should make prior generated directions unavailable until the user composes again.
entries.actual: Old Product Architecture and direction cards remained available after editing the brief or Visual Ambition, so the user could open a project that did not match the current form.
reproduction: Compose a product brief and wait for all three direction cards.
Edit the brief or change Visual Ambition.
Before the fix, the original directions remained visible and actionable.
entries.rootCause: The output was gated only by a hasComposed flag and catalogue readiness; the rendered controls were not compared with the input snapshot used for composition.
entries.remediation: Fingerprint the normalized brief and all composition controls at submit. Hide stale output and announce that the user must compose again when the fingerprint changes.

regression.before: Separate visible UI browser tests failed on the old source: both editing the brief and changing Visual Ambition left the previous direction cards available; the setting-specific run produced no stale-state status.
regression.after: The 16-run desktop/mobile suite hides stale directions after either a brief or setting change and announces that recomposition is required.

entries.title: Compose toggle choices did not expose their selected state
entries.expected: Visual Ambition, Structural Creativity, and target-device choices should expose their current selection to keyboard and assistive-technology users.
entries.actual: Selected buttons changed color but had no pressed state or named toggle group.
reproduction: Open /compose and focus a Visual Ambition or Structural Creativity stop.
Use Enter or Space to select a different stop.
Before the fix, the visual style changed but aria-pressed was absent.
entries.rootCause: The controls were ordinary buttons with color-only selected styling and no grouped or pressed semantics.
entries.remediation: Add accessible labels to toggle groups and expose each selected state through aria-pressed while preserving existing keyboard button interaction.

regression.before: Desktop and mobile checks found selected controls without aria-pressed.
regression.after: Enter and Space operate the toggles, the selected state is announced, and the 390px Compose document has no horizontal overflow.

entries.title: Last selected target device looked active but silently refused removal
entries.expected: A user should understand that at least one target device must remain selected and the final selected control should not look actionable.
entries.actual: The final selected device button remained enabled and visually active; clicking it caused no state change and gave no explanation.
reproduction: Open Advanced Constraints & Devices.
Remove devices until one remains.
Click the remaining selected device; before the fix, it remained selected without feedback.
entries.rootCause: The toggle handler prevented an empty target list, but the view did not reflect that invariant or explain the refused interaction.
entries.remediation: Disable the final selected device button, expose pressed state for all device toggles, and announce the minimum-one-device rule.

regression.before: The last selected device remained enabled and no explanation appeared.
regression.after: The last selected device is disabled and a status message explains the constraint on both desktop and mobile.

entries.title: Selecting a valid sample brief left the previous input error visible
entries.expected: Loading a valid sample brief should clear the empty-brief alert and invalid field state.
entries.actual: After an empty submission, selecting the Playful HR Platform sample updated the brief but left the prior error visible.
reproduction: Open /compose and submit a whitespace-only brief.
Select the Playful HR Platform sample brief.
Before the fix, the validation alert and aria-invalid state persisted beside a valid description.
entries.rootCause: The manual text-input handler cleared the validation error, but the separate sample-brief selection handler updated form state without clearing validation state.
entries.remediation: Clear the validation error when a valid sample brief is selected and verify the alert and invalid state disappear.

regression.before: The visible regression failed: one alert remained after the valid sample was selected.
regression.after: The test passes on desktop and mobile; the alert is removed and aria-invalid is cleared.

entries.title: Canvas taps on disabled resource actions did not select the resource
entries.expected: Tapping a disabled resource action in the canvas should select its containing node and open Inspect without activating the disabled action.
entries.actual: The disabled Explore Interface System button swallowed the pointer interaction, leaving the mobile Workbench on Preview with no selected node.
reproduction: Compose the employee-experience brief, open Direction C in Workbench, and switch to Settings & Policies.
Tap the disabled Explore Interface System button in the canvas.
Before the fix, Preview remained active and the inspector showed no selected node.
entries.rootCause: Native disabled controls suppress the click event used by the Workbench canvas selection handler, so the containing resource node never received selection.
entries.remediation: Capture pointerdown on the containing resource node when its target is disabled, prevent the disabled action, and select the node. Keep the action disabled until it has a connected behavior.

regression.before: The visible mobile regression failed at the inspector assertion when the disabled resource action was tapped.
regression.after: The visible mobile regression passes; the same tap selects the containing component, opens Inspect, and the action remains disabled.

entries.title: Composition flattened resource kinds into section nodes
entries.expected: Composed resource nodes should preserve the catalogue kind in ProjectManifest.nodeType so the Workbench exposes layout, section, block, component, and element hierarchy accurately.
entries.actual: The composition pipeline assigned section to every non-navigation resource, so block, component, and primitive resources appeared as sections and the generated tree contained no truthful component or element levels.
reproduction: Compose the exact employee-experience brief through /compose and open Direction C in Workbench.
Inspect the visible Layers tree and select resource-backed nodes.
Before the fix, an entity-profile-header block was serialized with nodeType section; the type contract regression failed.
entries.rootCause: composeProjectForDirection hard-coded section for every resource-backed node except navigation, discarding ResourceManifest.resourceType.
entries.remediation: Derive the editor node type from the selected catalogue resource type, with navigation retained as layout, then verify the visible tree and inspector expose root, section, component, and element selection.

regression.before: The new composer contract test failed because a block resource was emitted as section.
regression.after: The composer contract and desktop/mobile visible selection journeys pass with resource-kind-preserving nodes.

entries.title: Project DNA values were labelled inherited
entries.expected: When no node is selected, Design DNA status labels should identify the project as the value source. Node scopes should continue to distinguish inherited, overridden, and locked values.
entries.actual: The Feel Mixer, Visual Ambition, and Structural Creativity all displayed INHERITED while Project Scope was active, even though those values were the project-level source.
reproduction: Compose the exact employee-experience brief, open Direction C, and open the Workbench at 1440×900.
Select any node, then use Deselect Node to enter Project Scope.
Inspect the Feel Mixer, Visual Ambition, and Structural Creativity status badges. Before the fix all seven badges read INHERITED.
entries.rootCause: FeelMixer and IntentTab treated a missing selected node as the inherited state instead of as the project-level source scope.
entries.remediation: Render Project at project scope, Inherited or Overridden at an editable node scope, and Locked where a local or ancestor lock applies. A browser regression checks all seven project-scope labels and representative mobile inheritance.

regression.before: The visible desktop assertion failed because the Project label was absent and the seven values were reported as inherited.
regression.after: Desktop shows seven Project labels at Project Scope; mobile shows the Project source and inherited child value. Both runs report zero console errors, warnings, uncaught exceptions, failed requests, and HTTP errors.

entries.title: DNA lock snapshot behavior was not explained after unlocking
entries.expected: The lock control should explain that a lock preserves current effective DNA as local values and that Reset to Inherited resumes ancestor values after unlocking.
entries.actual: Lock Design DNA only said it protected overrides during global recomposition. After unlock, inherited values appeared as local overrides and required an explicit reset without explaining why.
reproduction: In Workbench, select a node inheriting from its parent and lock Design DNA.
Change the parent value while the child remains locked, then unlock the child.
Observe that the child retains its frozen value as an override and that Reset to Inherited restores the new parent value.
entries.rootCause: The lock description documented protection during recomposition but omitted that the frozen effective values remain local after unlock until explicitly reset.
entries.remediation: Explain the snapshot and reset behavior in the Lock Design DNA control and name the ancestor inheritance behavior in the reset tooltip. The visible browser regression verifies locked, overridden-after-unlock, and inherited-after-reset states.

regression.before: The visible test expected immediate inheritance after unlock and received the frozen snapshot; the saved screenshot showed six DNA properties marked Overridden and a Reset to Inherited control with no explanation.
regression.after: The Locks panel explains snapshot persistence. The desktop regression confirms the frozen child value remains local after unlock, then Reset to Inherited picks up the changed parent value with no runtime or network errors.

entries.title: Duplicating a screen could produce an invalid project route
entries.expected: Every duplicate screen should receive a unique route and fresh screen/node identities so the manifest remains valid.
entries.actual: Two rapid duplicates of the root route both appeared as Marketing Home (Copy) at /-copy. The visible UI accepted both and the downloaded manifest failed canonical validation for duplicate routes.
reproduction: Open the Playful HR showcase in Workbench at 1440x900.
Open Pages and duplicate Marketing Home twice.
Inspect the two copy rows and export the manifest.
entries.rootCause: The duplicate handler always appended a fixed -copy suffix and copy name without checking existing screens. For root route /, both copies therefore became /-copy. Screen IDs were also derived from millisecond timestamps, which risked collisions under rapid duplication.
entries.remediation: Normalize the source route with the screen name as the root fallback, allocate a unique copy suffix from the current screens, use createId for screen identities, and verify the downloaded manifest against ProjectManifestSchema.

regression.before: The visible regression failed: both copies had route /-copy, and canonical manifest validation returned false.
regression.after: Two copies receive /marketing-home-copy and /marketing-home-copy-2; screen/node IDs and routes are unique, and the exported manifest validates.

entries.title: Add Page accepted a route already assigned to another screen
entries.expected: The Add Page form should reject a normalized route collision, show an accessible error, and leave the screen list unchanged.
entries.actual: Submitting /people created an eighth screen even though /people already belonged to People Directory; no alert explained the collision.
reproduction: Open the Playful HR showcase in Workbench at 1440x900.
Open Pages, choose Add Page, enter a new title and /people as the route.
Submit and observe that the duplicate route is added without an error.
entries.rootCause: The Add Page handler normalized slashes and case for display but did not compare the candidate route with routes already in the manifest before calling addScreen.
entries.remediation: Normalize both existing and proposed routes, reject a duplicate before mutation, and render a role=alert message. The regression checks that the count remains 7 for /people and that a unique route can then be added.

regression.before: The baseline browser run showed screen count 7 before submit and 8 after; the expected alert was absent.
regression.after: The browser run shows count 7 before and after /people, exposes an accessible collision message, then accepts /people-route-check.

entries.title: Tree mutation engine actions were not reachable from the Layers UI
entries.expected: A selected non-root layer should expose usable duplicate, sibling move, and confirmed delete actions; invalid root and locked operations should be disabled with an explanation.
entries.actual: The Layers panel exposed selection, expansion, and lock toggles, but no Duplicate, Move, or Delete controls. Playwright could not find the expected root-disabled Duplicate action.
reproduction: Open the Playful HR showcase in Workbench at 1440x900.
Select Layers and select the screen root.
Observe the missing selected-layer action group; repeat with a non-root layer.
entries.rootCause: The mutation executor supported INSERT_NODE, MOVE_NODE and DELETE_NODE, but LayersTab rendered only lock toggles and did not connect those operations to user controls.
entries.remediation: Expose actions for selected non-root nodes through the existing mutation/history path; preserve root/ancestor-lock guards, require a second delete action, provide keyboard selection and visible status, and document that Move is sibling-only.

regression.before: The baseline browser run failed because the selected root had no Duplicate action or disabled-state explanation.
regression.after: Desktop and 390x844 browser checks verify root/lock guard messages, keyboard selection, duplicate/move/delete, exact undo/redo, schema-valid export, and action reachability above the mobile navigation.

entries.title: Workbench mutation capabilities were inaccurately classified
entries.expected: Each advertised mutation verb should have distinct observable semantics, or be labelled experimental and excluded from Core workflows.
entries.actual: Improve, Simplify, Intensify, and Match DNA appeared as Beta rows despite lacking separate deterministic operation contracts; no corresponding mutation controls existed in the Workbench. The visible selected-layer actions exposed only concrete duplicate, sibling move, delete, lock and unlock controls.
reproduction: Review the Step 19 mutation inventory and Workbench mutation specification.
Compare the listed Improve, Simplify, Intensify and Match DNA operations with the visible Workbench controls and mutation schema.
Observe that no operation-specific behavior or acceptance criteria are defined.
entries.rootCause: Natural-language intent labels were recorded as shipped mutation features without an operation-specific target, output contract, or observable result.
entries.remediation: Classify these verbs as Lab until their behavior and safety criteria are defined, keep unsupported natural-language proposals out of production mutation controls, and record Hide as Lab because ProjectNode has no persisted visibility field.

regression.before: The inventory and Workbench contract described unsupported verbs as Beta or as available layer actions.
regression.after: The inventory and matrix mark the unspecified verbs Lab, and the Workbench contract lists only implemented controls and their limits.

entries.title: Mobile Workbench hid structural-action results outside the Command tab
entries.expected: After Recompose or Surprise Me, the Workbench should announce the completed action and its outcome on the current mobile tab.
entries.actual: The manifest changed and locked content remained intact, but the success explanation was rendered only inside CommandBar, which is not mounted while Pages or other mobile tabs are active.
reproduction: At 390x844, open the Playful HR showcase in Workbench and select Pages.
Lock the Team Overview KPI subtree, then click Recompose.
Export the manifest and confirm the workspace hierarchy changed while the locked KPI subtree remained identical; observe that no role=status feedback is visible.
Repeat with Surprise Me and observe that the manifest changes but the explanation is absent from the active tab.
entries.rootCause: MobileWorkbench mounted CommandBar only on the Command tab, while the store's lastActionMessage was consumed only by CommandBar. Other active tabs therefore hid feedback for successful top-toolbar mutations.
entries.remediation: Subscribe to the shared lastActionMessage in MobileWorkbench and render it as a polite status region below the toolbar on non-Command tabs. Keep the detailed message in CommandBar when that tab is active. Add desktop/mobile browser regressions for both structural actions and ensure the live status fits the viewport.

regression.before: Both mobile browser tests observed mutationApplied=true and feedbackVisible=false, then failed because no role=status element existed on the active Pages tab.
regression.after: Desktop and 390x844 browser tests confirm the status region announces Recompose and Surprise Me, remains within viewport bounds, and the resulting manifests preserve locked subtrees, resolve all catalogue resources, and undo/redo exactly.

entries.title: Undo and redo history disappeared after reloading a local project
entries.expected: After a project edit is saved locally, refreshing Workbench should preserve the bounded undo and redo stacks so the user can restore exact recent states.
entries.actual: The latest manifest remained available after reload, but Workbench reset history and future to empty arrays. Undo was disabled despite 51 visible Design DNA edits immediately before reload.
reproduction: At 1440x900 or 390x844, open the Playful HR showcase in Workbench and open Project Scope > Intent.
Use the Visual Ambition slider to create 51 sequential keyboard edits; export the final manifest and verify the slider reads 51.
Reload the Workbench URL. The manifest remains at 51, but Undo is disabled and none of the prior states can be restored.
entries.rootCause: WorkbenchShell persisted the current ProjectManifest and checkpoint journal, but not the in-memory history and future stacks. setManifest correctly reset those arrays on load, leaving the saved project without its recent edit history.
entries.remediation: Persist bounded, schema-validated history stacks in a versioned IndexedDB store using immutable snapshots and a small stack pointer; coalesce rapid UI edits so the newest state is durable before the save status reports Saved; restore history before enabling the loaded Workbench; cap checkpoint restoration to the same 50-step window; and show local history save state in the toolbar.

regression.before: The baseline desktop and mobile reports record 51 visible edits, a project manifest restored at ambition 51, and undoEnabledAfterReload=false. The browser regression failed on the disabled Undo control.
regression.after: Desktop and mobile browser tests preserve the 50-step history window across reload, undo all 50 edits to the exact retained manifest, redo all 50 to the exact final manifest, and restore a named checkpoint after another reload. Each report records zero console errors or warnings, uncaught exceptions, failed requests, and HTTP errors.

entries.title: Blending a project overwrote the source project history
entries.expected: Creating and reloading a blended project should leave its source project and undo history independently reloadable.
entries.actual: After Blend wrote source snapshots under the new project ID, reopening the source project entered recovery mode because one of its history snapshots had been overwritten.
reproduction: Open a Compose direction in Workbench and record its project URL and manifest.
Change Visual Ambition through the visible Intent control and wait for the local history status to report Saved.
Use Blend to create a new project, reload it, then reopen the source project URL.
The source project displays Local project needs attention with a missing undo history snapshot error.
entries.rootCause: History snapshot IDs were generated per manifest object but the IndexedDB key was global. When Blend reused a source manifest snapshot in the new project history, its record was overwritten with the blended project ownership metadata, so the source pointer referenced a missing record.
entries.remediation: Allocate each snapshot ID within its owning project scope and include that owner in the IndexedDB key. Keep the same manifest object mapped to distinct snapshot IDs when it belongs to multiple project histories.

regression.before: The visible-browser regression passed through Blend and blended-project reload, then failed when returning to the source project. The source UI entered recovery mode with a missing history snapshot. The baseline report records zero console errors, failed requests, or HTTP errors.
regression.after: The same desktop UI regression reloads the blended project, returns to the source project, confirms Undo is enabled, and undoes the source edit to its prior Design DNA value. The report records zero console errors, failed requests, or HTTP errors.
